identity.title: Regularized Maximum Likelihood Image Synthesis and Validation for ALMA Continuum Observations of Protoplanetary Disks
identity.journal: Publications of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific

paper_type_evidence.quote: To identify best practices for RML imaging, we used the GPU-accelerated open source Python package `MPoL`, a machine learning-based RML approach, to explore the influence of common RML regularizers
We used ALMA DSHARP observations of the protoplanetary disk around HD 143006 to compare the performance of `MPoL` and CLEAN

analysis_steps.goal: Rescale visibility weights of the DSHARP HD 143006 data

method.value: Build a tclean model, subtract it from the visibilities, and compare the scatter of the residuals with the Gaussian envelope expected from the thermal weights; multiply sigma by a per-spectral-window scale factor

evidence.quote: We found empirical weight scalings for each dataset by creating a `tclean` model, subtracting it from the visibilities, and examining the scatter in the visibility residuals compared to the Gaussian envelope expected from the thermal weights ($w=\sigma^{-2}$).

key_parameters.value: Scale factors per spectral window: minimum 1.46, maximum 1.91, average 1.75

evidence.quote: with a minimum scale factor of 1.46, a maximum of 1.91, and an average of 1.75 over all spectral windows

analysis_steps.goal: Grid the visibilities and make dirty images

method.value: Average ungridded visibilities onto a Fourier grid with as many cells as image pixels (weighted average, equivalent to uniform weighting)

evidence.quote: Before performing any imaging (either creating a dirty image or an RML image), we take the ungridded visibility data and average it to grid cells in the visibility domain.

key_parameters.value: RML images always begin with uniformly weighted visibilities

evidence.quote: RML images in `MPoL` always begin with uniformly weighted visibilities

analysis_steps.goal: Forward-model the image with RML in MPoL

method.value: Minimize a loss made of the negative log likelihood (chi^2/2) plus regularizer terms with lambda prefactors, by gradient descent with PyTorch auto-differentiation; pixel values mapped through Softplus for positivity; model initialised from the dirty image or other images

evidence.quote: We use gradient descent methods, which are iterative processes with several components.
We chose the Softplus function

evidence.quote: with a positive, uniform set of reference pixels ($\mathbf{I}=10^{-7} \; \rm{Jy \; arcsec}^{-2}$)

analysis_steps.goal: Tune lambda hyperparameters with K-fold cross-validation

method.value: K-fold CV with K=10, using random cell or dartboard partitioning of gridded visibilities; CV score is the sum of chi^2 on held-out folds

evidence.quote: In this study, we restricted our exploration of CV to K-fold CV with $K=10$.
Dartboard partitioning uses polar grid lines to create a new layer of azimuthal and radial bins, each of which contains many visibility grid cells.

key_parameters.value: 15000 iterations per fold; one CV score took about 11-12 minutes on an NVIDIA Tesla K80 GPU

evidence.quote: computing a single CV score ($K=10$, 15000 iterations each) took around 11-12 minutes on a NVIDIA Tesla K80 GPU

key_parameters.value: Random cell partitioning draws grid cells without replacement into K subsets

evidence.quote: Random cell partitioning utilizes $K$ subsets that are composed of randomly-selected visibility grid cells.

validation.value: Each fold must converge, otherwise the CV score is invalid

evidence.quote: If each K-fold does not reach convergence, the final CV score is invalid and the entire CV process must be repeated with enough iterations to ensure full convergence.

findings_qualitative.value: A combination of entropy, sparsity and TSV works well on HD 143006 and the synthetic disk; TV degrades fine detail

evidence.quote: a combination of entropy, sparsity, and TSV regularization works well, while TV regularization does not adequately retain fine details in the images

findings_qualitative.value: Many lambda values give comparably low CV scores, so a coarse grid suffices

evidence.quote: there commonly exists a range of hyperparameters that result in similar images

findings_qualitative.value: Over-regularized sparsity can remove diffuse emission and whole rings

evidence.quote: sparsity regularization with a high $\lambda$ value removed some of the more diffuse emission, and in extreme cases removed some rings entirely

claims.hypothesis: RML imaging with MPoL can improve resolution over CLEAN for ALMA disk continuum data without losing sensitivity
claims.experiment: Image DSHARP HD 143006 with entropy + sparsity + TSV and compare with the DSHARP CLEAN image
claims.result: RML recovers all CLEAN features with less background noise; resolution gain up to a factor of 3 (2-3 in conclusion)
claims.finding: RML improves angular resolution without sacrificing sensitivity

evidence.quote: finding that RML imaging improved the spatial resolution of the image by up to a factor of $3$ without sacrificing sensitivity

claims.hypothesis: Cross-validation can tune regularization strengths efficiently
claims.experiment: K=10 CV on HD 143006 and the synthetic disk with random cell and dartboard partitioning
claims.result: CV scores are loosely U-shaped with a range of lambda giving comparable scores
claims.finding: A coarse grid of lambda values is enough to identify good models

evidence.quote: found that CV over a coarse grid of regularization strengths easily identifies a range of models with comparably strong predictive power

claims.hypothesis: Which regularizers work best for disk continuum images
claims.experiment: Image HD 143006 and the synthetic disk with entropy, sparsity, TV and TSV alone and combined
claims.result: Entropy gives high resolution, sparsity removes background noise, TSV defines rings, TV degrades resolution
claims.finding: Entropy + sparsity + TSV is the preferred combination

evidence.quote: a combination of entropy, sparsity, and TSV regularization works well, while TV regularization does not adequately retain fine details in the images

claims.hypothesis: Random cell and dartboard CV partitioning give comparable tuned images relative to hand tuning
claims.experiment: Compare tuned RML images of the synthetic disk with the ground truth
claims.result: Random cell CV and hand tuning gave the images closest to truth; dartboard was slightly noisier
claims.finding: Both partitionings are viable, random cell slightly better

evidence.quote: We found that tuning by random cell CV or by eye achieved images closest to the ground truth, while dartboard partitioning resulted in a similar but slightly noisier image.

claims.hypothesis: RML recovers the true structure of a simulated disk
claims.experiment: RML imaging of the synthetic dataset compared with the input image in image and visibility space
claims.result: Prominent rings and gaps recovered; smallest scales and low-contrast variations not recovered; long-baseline extrapolation only partial
claims.finding: RML recovers main structure but not the finest scales

evidence.quote: but failed to suppress enough noise to recover features at the smallest spatial scales or with low contrast flux variations.

claims.hypothesis: A restoring beam is needed for RML images
claims.experiment: Convolve RML images with Gaussian beams of 1/4 to 3/2 of the tclean beam
claims.result: No qualitative differences for beams up to 1/2 of the tclean beam
claims.finding: A modest restoring beam of 1/3-1/2 nominal resolution is recommended but not required

evidence.quote: We recommend restoring the image to no more than 1/3 to 1/2 of the nominal resolution in order to retain the superresolution benefits of RML imaging.

why_this_data.value: HD 143006 chosen as a well-studied disk with potential small-scale structure

evidence.quote: We chose this protoplanetary disk because it is well-studied and has potential for structures at small spatial scales, including azimuthal asymmetries.

why_this_method.value: Regularizers avoid CLEAN drawbacks by adding information to image synthesis

evidence.quote: Many of the drawbacks encountered with CLEAN can be partially or completely avoided by using an alternative class of imaging techniques which incorporate additional information into the image synthesis routine through the use of regularizers.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: TV excluded from the final combined image because it degraded resolution

evidence.quote: but excluded TV because it degraded the resolution of the image.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Exponential mapping of pixel values rejected in favor of Softplus

evidence.quote: $I_i = \exp(Z_i)$ is another potential mapping function, however, we found the Softplus function hastened model optimization.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Run enough iterations for the loss to converge

evidence.quote: it is essential to use enough iterations so that the loss function fully converges on a solution.

limitations_admitted.value: RML images failed to recover the smallest-scale and low-contrast features of the synthetic disk

evidence.quote: but failed to suppress enough noise to recover features at the smallest spatial scales or with low contrast flux variations.

limitations_admitted.value: RML model only partly extrapolates to long baselines

evidence.quote: The model appears to interpolate well at $(u,v)$ that is already thoroughly sampled by the original data (i.e. $q<4000$), but only partially extrapolates to long baselines.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only one real disk (HD 143006) and one synthetic disk are tested, so the regularizer ranking may not generalize
The quoted resolution gain (up to 3 versus 2-3) has no stated measurement method
Final lambda values for entropy and sparsity are not reported, and the final lambda_TSV was tuned by eye
Ground truth comes from a simulation with a Hann-windowed, rescaled image and the same uv sampling, which favours RML
No uncertainty estimates on CV scores or on the resolution gain
